en.t: has had a tenth taken from him

01.r: Adds a further point to the argument.

02.r: With 'a word to say', forms the phrase 'so to speak'.

03.r: Part of the fixed phrase; it has no English of its own here.
03.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'a word' and cites only this verse, in the classical phrase ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, 'so to speak'. Literally 'as to say a word'.

04.r: The writer flags that what follows is a way of putting it, not a plain statement of fact.
04.n: The phrase softens the claim that Levi, not yet born, paid a tenth. The Geneva's 'to say as the thing is' appears to take it the other way, as an insistence that it is so.

05.r: Abraham is the channel through whom Levi paid.

06.r: Levi's forefather, who gave the tenth to Melchizedek.

07.r: Stresses the surprise: even Levi, the one who receives tenths.

08.r: The priestly tribe's ancestor, standing for the priests descended from him.
08.n: Abbott-Smith lists this verse under Levi the son of Jacob.

09.r: The article with the participle: Levi, the one who receives.

10.r: The tenth parts paid to the priests.
10.n: The same word as in Hebrews 7:8, rendered 'tenths' there too.

11.r: Present participle: through his descendants, Levi is the one who receives tenths.

s: has had a tenth taken from him
12.r: Levi, in Abraham, was the one from whom the tenth was taken.
12.n: The verb is the one rendered 'has taken a tenth from' in Hebrews 7:6, here in the perfect passive: literally 'has been tithed'. Abbott-Smith gives the passive as 'to pay tithe' and cites this verse, which is how every translation here renders it.
